newsitem.title: CANADA: Sun Media CEO says no "for sale" sign on Post.
newsitem.headline: Sun Media CEO says no "for sale" sign on Post.

text.p: Sun Media Corp chief executive Paul Godfrey said on Wednesday there are no "for sale" signs on any of the company's assets, including the Financial Post.
"I would not jump to any conclusion about anything that remains in the Sun corporation," Godfrey said in a telephone interview.

Rumors have been rampant that the Financial Post daily business tabloid may be sold in the near future as the management group which completed its takeover of the Sun group earlier this month struggles to contend with a mountain of debt.
"We have received inquiries about almost every property that we continue to own save and except for my wife and children," Godfrey joked.
"So this is a very desirable group of newspapers. I am not prepared to entertain at this point in time discussions on any aspect of selling any part of it," he added.

Godfrey and his management team won the Sun chain, which includes tabloids in Toronto, Ottawa, Edmonton and Calgary, early in October. The buyout, which cost about C$411 million, piled about C$250 million in debt on to the once debt-free Sun group.
Conrad Black's Hollinger Inc and Torstar Corp are two names that analysts have bandied about as likely buyers for the Post if it should go on the block.
But Godfrey declined to discuss specific companies that might have expressed interest.
"There are no 'for sale' signs out on any of our properties and I am not going to get into a speculative situation," Godfrey said.
-- Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com
